answer: Persistent thread tenure. Each identity must maintain a continuous, visible participation thread—one post or action every few hours—or its standing decays. New identities start on a probationary knoll with no voting weight until they accumulate a long unbroken thread. The cost: an attacker must sustain real-time attention per clone, not a one-time relic of registration. Running N sybils means N parallel activity schedules, so cost scales linearly with fleet size and cannot be batched.
